output.answer_markdown: Restructuring and other decreased by $291 million in 2023 compared to 2022, primarily because of a gain on the sale of a divested business, partially offset by restructuring charges, asset impairment charges, and fair value adjustments on loans and interest receivable held for sale [1]. The gain came from the Happy Returns sale, which was completed in the fourth quarter of 2023 and recorded a pre-tax gain of $339 million, net of transaction costs [2]. The 2023 global workforce reduction added restructuring charges of $122 million [3].
